input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at indemnitor's expense, control of defence, no prejudicial settlement without consent) appears at 20.4, and 20.5 provides the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies without cutting off the defence obligation. Customer's reciprocal indemnity at 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and combinations. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity is not subject to the general liability cap — better than the fallback super-cap. No redline required.
